prompt: Two bonds are identical in all respects except that Bond A is callable and Bond B is non-callable. Which of the following best describes their relationship?

options.A: Bond A has a higher yield and higher price than Bond B.
options.B: Bond A has a higher yield and lower price than Bond B.
options.C: Bond A has a lower yield and lower price than Bond B.

explanation: A callable bond gives the issuer the right to redeem it early, typically when interest rates fall. This option is valuable to the issuer and harmful to the bondholder — it caps upside price appreciation and creates reinvestment risk. To compensate investors for this embedded option, callable bonds must offer a higher yield than otherwise identical non-callable bonds. The higher yield directly implies a lower price. Price of callable bond = Price of non-callable bond − Value of call option. So Bond A has a lower price (option-adjusted spread is wider) and higher yield than Bond B.
